summary: Built byte-exact encoders for all six small structured streams (Global/ElemTable, Global/History, Global/DocumentIncrementTable, Global/PartitionTable, Contents, BasicFileInfo) as decode->plain-dict-model->encode pairs; encode(decode(payload)) == payload byte-for-byte for 36/36 (six streams x six corpus files). The 8-byte Global/* per-name constant prefix (Latest=5, CD/DIT/History=1, ElemTable/PartitionTable=0) is an explicit separate step (global_prefix / wrap_global_stream); page framing defers to rvt.ecc.page_trailer via an import stub (zero placeholder + ecc_valid=False until the ECC fleet lands). Mutation helpers (streams_edit) implement id allocation (watermark+1), sorted ElemRec insertion, History episode append (prepend newest-first), DIT save-record append with the observed counter/G/id_pair progression, Contents counter mirror, BasicFileInfo increment/GUID/mirror-regeneration, a coordinated record_save(), and a save_impact(N) report of what must change vs stays constant when N elements are added. No wave-1 decoder file was modified; lossy spots were closed inside my own decode_* wrappers (History pad10/pad_u32, DIT records2 second copy, an independent lossless Contents decoder, BFI mirror/worksharing text) — all added bytes are constant zeros/derivable in 6/6 files.
key_findings: Round-trip byte-exact 36/36: ElemTable, History, DocumentIncrementTable, PartitionTable, Contents (payload + 24-byte prologue), BasicFileInfo (raw, with the UTF-16 mirror text REGENERATED from fields) all PASS on all six samples; full test suite 147 passed.

BasicFileInfo's human-readable mirror block is a fixed 19-line template that regenerates byte-exact from the binary fields in all six files, so a writer changing last_save_path / increments / GUIDs gets a consistent stream automatically.

Cross-stream save invariants verified 6/6: History count == max(ElemRec.modified_ep)+1; DIT newest id_pair == (History count-1, History count); BFI 'Unique Document Increments' == central_version_number == DIT record count; BFI Unique Document GUID == History entry[0]; Contents.counters == newest DIT counters with index 7 removed and Contents.G == DIT G; Partitions header count == ElemTable count.

DIT per-save progression across 160 consecutive record pairs in the corpus: counters[1..9] = previous+1 with index 7 gated by flag (160/160), counter_g +1 (160/160), sequence +1, only the newest record carries elem_id_repeat != 0 (== its (-1,X) value ~ partition element-record count, racbasic 85,814); the extra (key,0) pair appended to superseded records is (own sequence,0) in only 88/160 -> flagged hypothesis.

ElementId allocation: the ElemTable footer u64 is a monotonic highest-ever-issued watermark (racbasic watermark 1,098,947 vs max id 1,098,851 = 96 ids issued to since-deleted elements; equal in the other five files) -> next_element_id = watermark + 1 (direction verified; the off-by-one convention is the one open point).
PartitionTable id_b == the FIRST DIT record's id_pair.a in 6/6 files (workset created-at episode); filed to docs/inbox/stream-encoders.md.

GraveyardRec (count 0 corpus-wide) and worksharing-enabled BasicFileInfo text are unobserved: the ElemTable encoder refuses a non-empty graveyard and the BFI model carries an overridable worksharing_text rather than guessing.

open_questions: Off-by-one of the id allocator: is the footer watermark 'last issued' (next = wm+1, adopted) or 'next free' (next = wm)? Static files only prove wm >= max issued; needs an acceptance probe once ECC lands.
GraveyardRec wire layout (u32 count is 0 in all six samples) — encoder deliberately refuses a non-empty graveyard.

Meaning of the 10 DIT counters, hdr5, the flag=0 saves' small (-1) values, and the (key,count) pairs appended to superseded increment records (own-sequence rule only 88/160); does Revit require the DIT/Contents counters to be internally consistent with the object graph at all?
BasicFileInfo mirror text for worksharing_state != 0 (all corpus files 'Not enabled'); the model carries worksharing_text as an override.
Whether Revit tolerates a Contents stream without the ~42 bytes of stale trailing slack (reader should stop at the gzip trailer) — unverifiable until ECC-valid files can be tested.
